subject: Intrinsic functions
notes: PARTIAL -> CONFORMS (kb/Work PB251, landed). Both costs the refuter recorded are now paid, and neither was paid by argument. (1) THE SINGLE-SEAM PREMISE IS REPLACED BY A DECLARED CONTRACT PER SEAM. The refuted record read one intake and generalised; the file carried several with different value semantics. IntrinsicRenderer's 'Argument rendering' banner now names the vocabulary -- EXACT / LIFTED / ALIGNED / LANDED / INTEGRAL / APPROXIMATED / PREDICATE, each defined by what it does to the argument's VALUE -- and every member that reaches num.AsNum( declares its class in its own doc comment. IntrinsicArgumentIntakeContractDriftTests reads the renderer source, finds those members mechanically, and fails if one declares nothing, so a SIXTH seam is a red test rather than a hole in a list; a second test pins that Arg is the ONLY LANDED intake, which is the one that can redefine a value. The guard was PROVED to fail once (a marker removed from RawArg -> 'these IntrinsicRenderer members call num.AsNum( and declare no INTAKE(<class>) contract: RawArg'), so its green is evidence. (2) INSTANCES OF THE RULE ARE NOW TRACED AND PINNED. conformance:cases/15.4.1-Numeric-and-integer-functions/pb251_implementor_defined_argument puts the two numeric sources of an implementor-defined VALUE (RANDOM -- 15.75.4 r1 'The returned value is greater than or equal to zero and less than one'; SECONDS-PAST-MIDNIGHT -- 15.80.3 r2 seconds past midnight with r3's implementor-specified precision) in argument positions and asserts DETERMINISTIC consequences of each argument's own domain rule: INTEGER-PART(RANDOM) = 0 and INTEGER(RANDOM) = 0 over [0,1) (15.49.4 r1's equivalent arithmetic expression SIGN*INTEGER(ABS), and 15.44.4 r1's greatest-integer rule); MAX(RANDOM,2) = 2 and MIN(RANDOM,-1) = -1 by 15.59.4 r1 / 15.63.4 r1's pure selection, which is the plainest form of the propagation this NOTE describes since the returned value IS one argument's content; MAX(SECONDS-PAST-MIDNIGHT,86400) = 86400 and MIN(...,-1) = -1 over the [0,86400) domain 15.80.3 r2/r4 fix when the LEAP-SECOND ON directive is absent; INTEGER-PART(SECONDS-PAST-MIDNIGHT) in [0,86399]. Measured stable across three consecutive runs. Nothing over-defines an implementor-defined argument's result, which is the only way this latitude statement can be contradicted. Citations re-checked with cite.py --check: 15.75.4 r1 OK, 15.80.3 r2 OK, 15.80.3 r3 OK, 15.59.4 r1 OK, 15.63.4 r1 OK, 15.44.4 r1 OK.
